newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/OEX call buyers emerge.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/OEX call buyers emerge.

text.p: Wednesday's call sellers in the S&P 100 index turned to buyers Thursday as the market struggled to hold its ground.
"There were some big (call) sellers yesterday, but moderate buyers today," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in OEX options.
"We've had moderate size call orders."
He said that, overall, volumes were on the light side.
By about 1150 CDT/1650 GMT, the spot OEX was up a fraction at at 938.61. The broader S&P 500 index .SPX was also up fractionally at 960.76.
The big volume in OEX options was in the September 970 calls, which traded nearly 9,400 contracts.
Callahan said there were buyers of those options.
Other busy OEX calls included the August 940s, the August 950s and the August 960s.
On the put side, the August 860s traded nearly 4,500 contracts, the August 930s traded 3,100 and the August 920s traded about 2,600.
Traders said a sizable OEX August call exercise on Wednesday held few implications for the market going into next week's expiration.
Nearly 7,000 OEX calls were exercised and all were deep- in-the-money.
"A lot of premium has come out of the calls," Callahan said. "The deeps (in the money) have gone to parity pretty quickly."
Parity means the option is trading at its intrinsic value.
Callahan said more of those kinds of exercises would be likely leading into the expiration.
"I don't think it means anything," Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said of the large exercise.
He explained that the only way to get out of such deep-in-the-money calls was to exercise them because of tight liquidity.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said the big exercise put pressure on the market but that's about all.
"It's a judgement that the market's going to come in in the next week," he added. "They might be wrong but it's still a judgement."
In other activity, traders said SPX options activity was moderate, with a big trade in an out-of-the-money September call gaining scant attention.
The SPX September 1,025 call traded 9,810 contracts. The September 995 call traded 5,815 adn the September 1,010 call traded 2,360.
"It was no big deal," one trader said of the September 1,025 call, explaining it was part of a spread.
